report:
The retained PARTIAL scope is correct under its stated contact hypotheses and conditional geometric witness antecedents. This verdict does not close P16.1 or establish singular EP. No supplied draft or note was treated as granted background.

For n1, original-ring section localization works without normality: localization commutes with the finite matching conditions on an affine trivializing cover. The extra factor s in a=s∏τ_i preserves the original boundary. Clipped section-ideal logarithms give exact logarithms near the tested compact set. On the specified rational domains, density in the localized original ring and the strict ultrametric approximation inequality give identical unit norms, including after complete field extension. Ducros supplies precisely the compact Γ-strict norm-image theorem required here. Refinement by branch-equality hyperplanes, rational triangulation, affine interpolation and the finite wall penalty establish the polyhedral extension and DC decomposition. The cutoff, maximum-penalty gluing, clipping and saturation partition use lattice operations, with no multiplication of variable PL functions. Padding the finite FS decompositions by the canonical zero metric gives differences in one actual ample rational bundle, with the original cocycle and reference.

The continuous contact bridge correctly constructs the algebraic model before testing positivity. Relative integral closure preserves the nonnormal generic fiber. The flag-ideal identity holds at every Laurent analytic point because the homogeneous generators remain separate generators; it is not merely a Gauss-section identity. Unit-log supports pull back to harmonic functions. The same-constant contact equality proves the harmonic maximum test. The supplied harmonic-test proof can be checked directly, and decreasing subharmonic limits follow from compact boundary comparison; bounded floors exclude the identically −∞ case. The harmonic analytic inputs are corroborated by Wanner’s accessible primary treatment. GR is applied to already represented PL weights and tests curves throughout ordinary neighborhoods. Its residual-curve argument retains properness, the generic reduction point and the interior condition. GM consequently detects nefness of the represented model before field extension. BE interpolates models of the same generic bundle. The coefficient expansion at the independent-variable Gauss lift has an exact finite cutoff: canonical coefficient norms are at most one, while the continuous FS potential has a uniform finite lower bound. A common zero of the retained coefficients would contradict that bound. Thus the descended approximants use the original mL and rational weights.

For n2, the collar construction retains v=h₀+p and Φ=p+Ψ/A. Compact decreasing superlevel-set emptiness supplies a common eventual tail on the entire outer strip; this does not require uniform convergence to a discontinuous limit. On the inner open, u=AΦ+Ah₀+M+1, so the raw mixed product carries Aⁿ. A third shared collar proves independence using continuous compatibility followed by genuine decreasing convergence. Weighted convergence treats the genuine potential and fixed continuous reference separately. The correct pairing identity is test-containing pairing minus zero-test pairing; translating the test below zero permits the positive weighted-measure lemma to be applied to its negative.

Compact signed IBP is valid. The two positive measures associated with q⁺ and q⁻ need not individually have controlled support. Their difference vanishes outside the support of a because q⁺=q⁻ there and genuine mixed locality applies. Matching-reference curvature cancellation is first checked continuously and then passed term by term through the bounded genuine limits. Symmetry of the global pairing gives IBP with the remaining collar factors and scaling retained. The partition telescope then proves raw intersection mass, rather than defining it by normalization. Borel strict-winning locality and displaced maxima give bounded comparison. Every BJ divisorial point admits an ample-model measure with atom b_E(ℒ|E)ⁿ>0 before any inverse Dirac equation is invoked. Mixing with this bounded FS potential, comparison and equal mass prove local domination. Divisorial order follows through shared genuine truncations, rather than density plus usc.

The EP membership argument establishes first membership correctly. Continuous majorants form a decreasing net on the possibly nonmetrizable compact analytification. EP gives continuous genuine envelopes; orthogonality and the independently established local domination place the original bounded local potential below each envelope. Decreasing closure gives membership. Smooth characteristic-zero EP supplies the smooth instance. Floors and varying-class closure extend it to the stated unbounded and nef cases with actual semipositive references. Sequential regularization is used only afterwards.

For n3, the geometric compactification, projective birational domination and resolution witness remain conditional hypotheses. They are not inferred analytically. The boundary sign mπ*D−E, the exhaustion g=g₀+p, original-generator localization and upper-growth estimate are correct. Whole boundary collars give genuine membership for the nef truncations on the smooth witness. Birational descent uses approaching EP on the smooth target, exactly as BJ 5.13 requires. Subsequent FS regularization uses the same actual bundle, and dominated complete-system branches retain the original generators without changing values. Expanding collars decrease on the old region, the new annulus and the exterior separately. Their upper controls give a common bound for the regularized sequence. Principal-open logarithmic penalties have the asserted vanishing behavior near the removed set. Their removal uses decreasing tail envelopes, not a falsely decreasing sequence in c. Equality with the original weak input is proved in both directions on the same resolved witness: its divisorial points have generic algebraic support and therefore lie over Y_f. Shared floors and collars then identify every removed and exceptional value.

The nonflat norm argument is self-contained and correct. Normality of A puts the generic norm and characteristic coefficients in A[T]. Universal polynomial identities and right exactness of specialization handle new fiber relations. After algebraic closure, the norm character is trivial on nilpotent units and is a residue-torus monomial. Cayley–Hamilton makes every exponent strictly positive. Multiplication by separable residue degrees gives canonical positive integer weights totaling d, compatible with complete residue-field extensions. Weighted Gauss multiplicativity holds at arbitrary positive radii by the unique maximal lexicographic contribution. This proves the whole-base finite AFS formula. The lattice-density argument and the degree bound prove continuity for continuous inputs; indicator traces are locally constant, not necessarily constant on disconnected opens. In the diagnostic example, the origin has weight two despite fiber dimension three.

Harmless wording clarifications are required. “Smooth projective morphism” in Section 7 should read “projective birational domination with smooth projective source,” as required by the stated resolution-witness antecedent and BJ 5.13. Logarithms asserted harmonic are logarithms of units. The H/A switch in BE 7.8 is a naming typo. The reversed signs in BJ 7.21(ii) must be read with the corrected pairing order stated above. Positive-dimensional IBP formulas are understood for n≥1; for reduced irreducible zero-dimensional X, X is one point and the empty product has raw mass one. None of these clarifications requires a new substantive argument.

The mathematical limitations in n4 are accurate. The genuine reduced-projective finite-energy operator, its raw mass, intrinsic dual-energy condition and uniqueness are available independently of singular EP. [BJ Theorem 12.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4#page=121) makes onto finite-energy MA equivalent to EP. Its variational proof retains compactness, bounded-energy control, target integral continuity, energy usc and actual attainment. [Wu’s envelope proof](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27610v1#page=51) explicitly uses its resolved-nef descent and weak/global gates. The present argument leaves whole-base weak radial trace, Runge and singular induction, resolved-nef fiber descent, arbitrary-cardinality finite-data descent and normalization compatibility unfinished. The finite norm formula and smooth conditional gate do not supply those missing applications. Compilation, hashes and finite arithmetic observations play no role in this verdict.

passages.statement: For a reduced projective variety X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, BJ’s rational PL(X) is a vector lattice uniformly dense in C(Xan). Every rational PL potential on an actual rational line bundle L is represented by a test configuration of (X,L). Relative integral closure is taken inside its prescribed generic fiber and preserves that fiber; its local rings at generic points of the central fiber are DVRs. These are BJ Definition 1.10, Theorem 1.13, Theorems 2.2 and 2.7, and Theorem 2.31.
passages.quote: stable under finite maxima and minima

passages.statement: For a compact Γ-strict k-analytic space W of dimension d and invertible analytic functions f₁,…,f_r on W, Ducros Theorem 3.2 makes their norm image a finite (Q,(|k*|Γ)^Q)-polytope of dimension at most d. In its algebraic reduction, a Γ-rational domain in an algebraic affine analytification can be described using original-ring functions and a nonvanishing denominator h, and A[h⁻¹] is dense in that domain’s affinoid algebra.

For a reduced projective variety X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an actual ample rational line bundle H, every rational PL function is a difference of nonnegative rational multiples of FS potentials in H(H) (BJ 2.25–2.26). Every BJ divisorial valuation is a central-component valuation on a relatively integrally closed test configuration (Lemma 1.20). Any test configuration dominating the trivial configuration admits an ample model of any prescribed actual ample rational L (Lemma 2.33); its raw model measure has component coefficient ord_E(t)(ℒ|E)ⁿ.

On a smooth strictly analytic curve over an algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued field, harmonic functions on compact strictly affinoid domains are described by harmonic functions on semistable finite skeleta. The logarithm of the absolute value of an invertible analytic function is harmonic. Wanner gives this description in §5.3 and proves the unit-log assertion in Proposition 5.3.15.

Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, X a good strictly K-analytic space, and h an R-PL function. GR Corollary 5.4 says h is semipositive exactly when, over an algebraically closed analytic field extension F, h_F pulled back by every morphism from a smooth analytic curve over F is semipositive. On a smooth strictly analytic curve, R-PL semipositivity is equivalent to Thuillier subharmonicity (Proposition 5.1). Semipositivity at a point is equivalent to a nef formal representation on an ordinary strictly affinoid neighborhood.
passages.quote: for every smooth analytic curve C

passages.statement: For a formal metric on an actual line bundle over a separated paracompact strictly analytic space over a complete nontrivially valued field, semipositivity on ordinary point neighborhoods is equivalent to global formal semipositivity (GM Proposition 3.11). A represented formal metric is semipositive exactly when its representing line bundle is nef (Proposition 3.5). Nefness of a formal line bundle is equivalent to nefness after any complete analytic field extension (Lemma 3.3).
passages.quote: if and only if L is a nef formal K◦-model.

passages.statement: For an actual ample rational line bundle L on a projective scheme over a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field, a continuous metric is nef exactly when it is psh, and hence exactly when it is a uniform limit of pure FS metrics on the same L (BE Corollary 7.6 and Theorem 7.8). The proof approximates a nef model using an ample model with the same generic bundle.
passages.quote: Then a continuous metric on L is nef iff it is psh

passages.statement: On an n-dimensional projective scheme over a complete valued field, continuous psh-regularizable metrics on actual rational line bundles have symmetric positive mixed Radon measures, with raw mass equal to the fundamental-cycle intersection number, continuous under uniform convergence. Continuous FS-limit metrics on semiample bundles are psh-regularizable. Model Deligne pairings agree with algebraic model pairings, and the measures and pairings retain fundamental-cycle multiplicities and complete-field base-change compatibility (BE 7.14, 8.3–8.5 and 8.18–8.21).

Under CLD’s analytic-space hypotheses, if positive closed currents T_j converge to T and continuous functions u_{0,j},…,u_{q,j} converge locally uniformly to u₀,…,u_q, with u_{i,j} psh for i≥1, then u_{0,j} d′d″u_{1,j}∧…∧d′d″u_{q,j}∧T_j converges to u₀ d′d″u₁∧…∧d′d″u_q∧T. This is CLD Proposition 8.7.2.

For a reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, BJ’s genuine finite-energy pairing extends symmetrically and multilinearly to signed finite-energy entries and defines signed mixed Radon measures. For genuine psh entries these measures are positive, have raw intersection mass and satisfy the central-component model formula. They converge weakly along decreasing genuine finite-energy nets. If ω_i are ample, φ_i∈E¹(ω_i), and a psh test φ₀ is integrable for their mixed measure, decreasing approximations also converge as weighted measures; bounded other factors ensure that integrability. Genuine mixed measures agree on open sets where their potentials agree, and MA(max(φ,ψ)) agrees with MA(φ) on the Borel set {φ>ψ} for φ,ψ∈E¹(ω). These are BJ 7.14, 7.18–7.21 and 7.40–7.42.

For a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, θ∈N¹(X), φ∈PSH(θ), and an usc function ψ:Xan→R∪{−∞}, the inequality φ≤ψ holds on all of Xan if and only if it holds on BJ’s divisorial points. This is BJ Theorem 4.22.

For a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, a generically finite decreasing limit of φ_i∈PSH(θ_i), with θ_i→θ, belongs to PSH(θ). For an actual ample rational L, continuous genuine L-psh potentials are uniform limits of rational FS potentials on L, and every genuine L-psh potential admits a decreasing sequence in Hdom(c₁(L))⊂H(L). These are BJ 4.5, 4.7, 12.18(iii) and Example 3.9.

For an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and an ample class ω satisfying EP, the envelope P_ω(f) of a finite continuous function f is continuous and genuine ω-psh. Moreover, P_ω(f)=f almost everywhere for MA_ω(P_ω(f)). These are BJ Lemma 5.17 and Theorem 13.1, with their explicit EP hypothesis.

Every nef class on a smooth connected projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field has EP (BJ Theorem 5.20). For a projective birational morphism π:Y→X and θ∈N¹(X), if θ is the limit of target classes θ_m such that θ_m−θ is ample and θ_m has EP, then π*:PSH(X,θ)→PSH(Y,π*θ) is a homeomorphism, in particular onto (BJ Lemma 5.13).

For reduced irreducible projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field and ample ω, set V=(ωⁿ) and E_ω(φ)=⟨(ω,φ)ⁿ⁺¹⟩/((n+1)V). The genuine E¹ Monge–Ampère measure has raw mass V. A positive raw target ν of mass V has finite dual energy exactly when E_ω^∨(ν/V)=sup_{ψ∈E¹}(E_ω(ψ)−∫ψ d(ν/V)) is finite; this is equivalent to integrability of every genuine E¹ potential. Genuine solutions with the same measure differ by one real constant, and genuine domination holds without EP. The normalized genuine MA map onto all finite-dual-energy probability measures is surjective if and only if ω has EP. These are BJ 7.18–7.19, 9.20, 10.4, 10.6 and 12.8.
